info.title: emberhut
info.description: The HTTP/SSE API the Emberhut apps talk to. See docs/api.md.

post.summary:
A one-time code for a new device, made on a signed-in one. It works once, for 10 minutes.
With it comes the pairing link (`link`), for the app to show as a QR code.

200.description: A code, shown as ABCD-EFGH, and its pairing link

401.description: Not a signed-in device (in either auth mode)

post.summary:
Trades a one-time code for this device's own session. The answer names the machine (its id
and public key, for the device to pin). A device's own `publicKey` is taken and not kept:
it is stored only once the proof that the device holds it (`keySignature`) is checked.

400.description: No code, or a field the route refuses

401.description: A wrong, used or expired code

413.description: The body is over the server's limit

429.description: Too many wrong codes lately, for every caller

retry-after.description: Seconds until a code is taken again

post.summary: A new access token, and a new refresh token in place of the one sent.

400.description: A field the route refuses

401.description: The refresh token is not current: sign in again

413.description: The body is over the server's limit

get.summary:
The machine's signature over the probe's nonce and kind, and over how (`via`), where
(`local`) and as what (`host`) it was reached. No session is needed. Every answer carries
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so a page on any origin can check a route.

parameters.name: nonce
parameters.description: 32 fresh random bytes, base64url without padding.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: The kind of route the client is checking: 1 to 32 characters from `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`.

400.description: A nonce that isn't 32 bytes, a kind that isn't 1 to 32 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, or a request host that isn't one

404.description: A server without an identity of its own (a legacy host)

post.summary:
The machine's signed link to `account` at `relayDomain`, under its name, made now: the body
the desktop posts, as it is, to the directory's `POST /v1/machines`. Served only to a
signed-in device on this computer.

400.description: Not an account's user id or a relay domain

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

403.description: Not straight from a loopback TCP peer (another address, or passed on by a proxy, forward or relay)

404.description: A server without an identity of its own

413.description: The body is over the server's limit

get.summary: The state of a room. Sent back in `If-None-Match`, its `ETag` gets 304 while it is unchanged.

parameters.name: room
parameters.description: The room; none, or one the server doesn't know: Main.

parameters.name: if-none-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the state the client holds

parameters.name: x-emberhut-looking
parameters.description: The room on screen in front of the person, while it is

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

get.summary:
The room's live stream: the room as it is now, then each change, each event's data a
`LiveEvent` (a `Live` object while the assistant works, `null` when its turn ends); an
`approvals` event (`ApprovalsEvent`) when an approval request changes; a `: ping` comment
every 15 s on a quiet stream. Open until the client leaves or the server stops.

parameters.name: room
parameters.description: The room; none, or one the server doesn't know: Main.

200.description: A text/event-stream whose every unnamed event's data is a LiveEvent: a Live object while the assistant works, null when its turn has ended; an event named approvals carries an ApprovalsEvent when an approval request changes

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary:
Says something in a room. The message is stored at once; the reply comes with the next
polls and on the live stream.

200.description: Said; the assistant's turn has started

400.description: A body the route refuses, or a blank message without files the server stored

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

413.description: The body is over the server's limit

429.description: Eight messages in this room are waiting for an answer already

post.summary: A room's messages have been seen on screen: its `unread` clears.

400.description: A body the route refuses

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

413.description: The body is over the server's limit

get.summary: The thread's title, status and latest steps, read from the coding-thread app now.

parameters.name: machine
parameters.description: The machine, as the server names the coding-thread app there.

400.description: No coding-thread app on that machine (`ok: false`)

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

502.description: The coding-thread app could not be read: its error (`ok: false`)

get.summary: The document, as JSON. It is public: it describes the API, not anyone's data.

post.summary:
Does what the body's fields ask (several in one body run in a fixed order; a field no
action takes is left alone) and answers with the state of the body's room.

200.description: Done; the state of the body's room (Main by default)

400.description: An action refused or failed (`{ ok: false, error }`; the ones before it are done), or a body that isn't JSON

401.description: There is no session, and sign-in is enforced or an action needs a signed-in device (`authRevoke`, in either auth mode)

413.description: The body is over the server's limit

get.summary: The theme choice, its colours in both appearances, its contrast, and every preset's colours.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary:
Changes the fields given and answers the page as it is now; with `preview`, as it would be,
saving nothing.

400.description: A value the theme doesn't take, or a body that isn't JSON (`{ ok: false, error }`)

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

413.description: The body is over the server's limit

post.summary:
One MCP message (JSON-RPC 2.0) from a room's agent session: `initialize`, `ping`,
`tools/list` or `tools/call`. The bearer is the room's agent token, not a device's.

200.description: The request's answer: its result, or a JSON-RPC error (an unknown method). A tool call always has a result, `isError` when it failed

400.description: Not JSON, or not one JSON-RPC message (a JSON-RPC error)

401.description: No agent token, or not one the server issued

413.description: The body is over the server's limit (a JSON-RPC error)

501.description: The session is in a family member's room, or whose room it is can't be told: family rooms are not available yet

post.summary:
One MCP message (JSON-RPC 2.0) from a runner's session: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`
or `tools/call`, with a task's plan and the task in full as its only tools. The bearer is
the runner sessions' token, which the runners' shared MCP list hands out
(`GET /api/runner/mcp`); the session header names the calling session: one linked to tasks
writes only their plans, and a call naming none writes the task it names.

200.description: The request's answer: its result, or a JSON-RPC error (an unknown method). A tool call always has a result, `isError` when it failed

400.description: Not JSON, or not one JSON-RPC message (a JSON-RPC error)

401.description: Not the runner sessions' token this server process handed out (a token from before a restart is a stranger's)

413.description: The body is over the server's limit (a JSON-RPC error)

get.summary:
Up to 60 of a room's messages, oldest first: the newest before `before` (older messages,
for "Show earlier"), or the newest after `after` (what came since), or the newest of all.
A room that doesn't exist reads as Main.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only messages older than this one.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only messages newer than this one.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary:
Stores the file that is the request's body, as it arrives, under the name `?name=` gives
(none: `file`). The answer's file is sent back whole with the message it goes with.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
The file's name, extension included (`photo.png`): it decides the file's kind. Any text:
none is refused.

400.description: Not stored: over 500 MB, cut off, or the server couldn't write it

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

get.summary:
A file in the uploads folder, by the `url` of its chat file. With `Range: bytes=a-b`
(`a-` or `-n` too) only those bytes, as video players ask; a report (HTML) is served
sandboxed. Media players that can't send a header may put the token in `?token=`.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: One byte range: bytes=a-b, a- or -n

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

404.description: No such file

416.description: The range starts past the end of the file

get.summary:
Whether the server answers: `{ ok: true, lag }`. No sign-in, so a supervisor or a load
balancer can ask; it says nothing about anyone's data.

How late the server's runtime is, and the work that held it 50 ms or more in the last five
minutes, by name, the longest in all first.

200.description: The lag and the slow work

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

get.summary:
The sign-in mode, whether the server is in use, and whether this request comes from a
signed-in device. It answers with or without a session, in either mode, so an app can ask
before it has one; only a signed-in device is sent the device list.

Every item of the checklist and how it is: `ready`, `missing` (the owner can set it up
from the apps), `off` (it takes the server's own configuration) or `error` (set up, but
failing now), with a line saying how many there are or what to do. The Mac helper is asked
for its health, within 5 s; nothing else leaves the server.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

get.summary:
The provider saved, its key's last four characters, its base URL and models, when it last
accepted them, whether the agent can run on it, and whether it does now.

200.description: What is saved, without the key

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

put.summary:
Checks a provider (one request that needs the key, within 15 s; none for `claude`) and,
once it passes, saves it in place of whatever was saved, another provider's key removed.
The agent's sessions run on it from their next turn while no accounts are configured.

400.description: Not what the provider takes (a key, base URL or model missing or malformed); nothing was saved

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

422.description: The provider refused the key, or is too old to run the agent; nothing was saved

502.description: The provider didn't answer the check; nothing was saved

delete.summary:
Removes the saved provider and its key: the agent's next sessions run on the agent CLI's own
login.

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

post.summary:
Checks a provider as `PUT` does and lists its models, saving nothing: for choosing a model,
and for finding a local Ollama.

200.description: It let the server in; its models

400.description: Not what the provider takes

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

422.description: The provider refused the key, or is too old to run the agent

post.summary:
Keeps a signed-in phone's push address: an iPhone's APNs device token (with its service), or
an Android phone's FCM registration token. The same token again updates it.
post.description:
Signing the phone out forgets it. A session is needed in either auth mode: report mode's
pass for a request without one would let anyone who reaches the server have the replies
pushed to them.

200.description: Kept: the phone gets the alerts

400.description: Not a push token (`not a device token`, `not an FCM registration token`), or a body the route refuses

401.description: There is no session (in either auth mode)

413.description: The body is over the server's limit

get.summary: The form for a link's secrets.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The link's token: the link is the key

200.description: The form: one password field per secret, and why they are wanted

404.description: The link expired, was used, or never existed

post.summary: Saves the secrets typed into the form, each to its own file, and uses the link up.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The link's token: the link is the key

requestBody.description: The form's fields: each secret's name and what was typed

200.description: Saved what was filled in (or nothing); the link is used up

404.description: The link expired, was used, or never existed

get.summary:
The Mac's row: whether its helper answers (within 5 s), and then whether the screen is
locked and how long the Mac has been idle.

200.description: The Mac's row; `{ online: false }` alone when its helper doesn't answer or none is set up

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary: Locks the Mac's screen now. Nothing unlocks it.

400.description: Not locked: no Mac helper is set up, it doesn't answer (within 10 s), or it refused, as `error` says

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

get.summary:
The server's data: a consistent snapshot of the database (`emberhut.db`) and the files the
server keeps next to it, as one `.tar.gz`. The secrets directory is not in it (its keys are
kept and restored on their own), and one backup is made at a time.
get.description:
Only a signed-in device gets it, in either auth mode: it holds every message and the
hashes of every secret, and report mode's pass for requests without a session is not
meant for that. The database is snapshotted before the answer starts, so a failure there
is a 500; after that, a failure can only cut the archive short.

200.description: The backup, streamed: `emberhut.db` (the database's snapshot), then the data folder's files

content-disposition.description: attachment, with the file's name: emberhut-backup-<UTC day>.tar.gz

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

503.description: A backup is being made already; try again when it is done

get.summary:
Any task, done and canceled ones too: by key (`q=` a key or its number) or words of its
title and description, then the newest; filtered by project (`none`: no project), area,
statuses and owner; `closed=1` only done and canceled ones, `archived=1` only canceled ones.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A task's key, its bare number, or words of its title and description.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many (the default 50, at most 200).

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project's id, or `none` for tasks with no project.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Whose: the person's or the assistant's id.

200.description: The tasks found, at most `limit` (50; 200 at most)

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary:
A program on this machine hands the assistant a job the person asked it for: a task of the
assistant's with its brief, the person's request. Only with the server's program key as the
bearer, never a device's session.

400.description: No title or no body

401.description: Not the program key

get.summary: One task with everything its page shows: its history, subtasks, findings, links and runs.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

404.description: No such task

post.summary:
The person's reply on a task's page: it goes to the task (its worker, or the assistant told
to answer on the task), not the chat, and clears the ask.

400.description: Nothing to send, no such task, or a reply over 20 000 characters or 20 files

401.description: No signed-in device: a reply acts on the task, so it needs one in either mode

get.summary:
A file a task produced, by its artifact's id (never by its path), in byte ranges when asked
(videos stream and seek). A link, or a file that is gone, private or of a kind the app
doesn't open, is 404.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: One byte range: bytes=a-b, a- or -n

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

404.description: No such file

416.description: The range starts past the end of the file

get.summary: A small JPEG of a picture or a video a task produced, made once.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

404.description: No such picture or video, or no thumbnail could be made

get.summary: Everything with a next run, every room's, soonest first.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary:
Tells the assistant `text`: an event it reads at its next wake, in the room `project`
names when the server has it, in Main otherwise. A name (`Atlas`) is a room's name; a number
(`4` or `"4"`) is a project's id, its room, else a room's id.

200.description: Told; it wakes the room by the wake rule

400.description: No text (`{ ok: false, error: "text is required" }`), a text over 100 000 characters, a kind that isn't a plain word, or a body that isn't JSON

401.description: Neither a signed-in device nor the program key (in either auth mode)

413.description: The body is over the server's limit

get.summary: Every fact, most recently changed first, with the standing rules and the rules on trial.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

get.summary: Every quick note and diary entry, newest first.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary: Saves a quick note (new, or an edit by its `uid`); an empty `text` deletes it.

400.description: A note the diary doesn't take, or a body that isn't JSON (`{ ok: false, error }`)

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

413.description: The body is over the server's limit

post.summary:
One event from a runner about one of its sessions: the session and its turn as they are
now, so taking it twice changes nothing.

requestBody.description: The event: `{ machine, kind, at, session, turn?, ... }`

400.description: Not an event of this runner's

401.description: No runner's token

post.summary:
A runner's sample of its machine (every 20 s): kept as its latest and folded into its
5-minute point.

requestBody.description: The sample: `{ machine, host, platform, cpu, memory, gpus, disks, battery, runner, sessions }`

400.description: Not a sample of this runner's

401.description: No runner's token

get.summary:
The MCP servers the runners' sessions get too, as the server's operator listed them (none
when no list is configured). On a server that keeps tasks' plans, the list always has the
server's own entry: its runner sessions' endpoint, with the runner sessions' token and the
session header, so each session keeps its task's plan and its calls name the session. An
entry the operator listed for one of the server's own endpoints is kept instead, and gets the
session header (and, for the runner sessions' endpoint, the token) when it doesn't set them.

401.description: No runner's token

get.summary: Every runner machine's capacity, warnings, sessions and (unless `?history=0`) its last day.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

get.summary:
The runner sessions: a task's (`?task=`), a room's (`?room=`; Main: every room's), or the
person's own (`?direct`); newest first, 50 at most.

parameters.name: task
parameters.description: Only the sessions linked to this task.

parameters.name: room
parameters.description: Only this room's sessions (Main: every room's).

parameters.name: direct
parameters.description: Present: only the person's own sessions.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary:
One of the person's own sessions: on the machine and in the folder they picked (a worktree,
the account, model and effort if they chose them), their first message and files its first
turn.

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

409.description: Not started: no such runner, nothing to start with, or the runner's refusal (`ok: false`)

get.summary:
The folders on a runner's machine for the new-session sheet: where to start (no `path`), or
one folder's folders.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Folders: the folder to list (none: where to start).

parameters.name: cwd
parameters.description: Branches: the folder whose repository's branches to list.

400.description: No such runner (`ok: false`)

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

502.description: The runner refused or didn't answer (`ok: false`)

get.summary: The branches of the repository a folder on a runner's machine is in.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Folders: the folder to list (none: where to start).

parameters.name: cwd
parameters.description: Branches: the folder whose repository's branches to list.

200.description: The runner's listing: `{ repo, current, branches }`

400.description: No such runner (`ok: false`)

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

502.description: The runner refused or didn't answer (`ok: false`)

get.summary:
A runner session's transcript: the runner's steps after `?after=` (the newest `?limit=`,
400 by default, without one), with what the server knows of the session.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only the steps after this one.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many (400 by default, 1000 at most).

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: A worker's: only this sub-agent call's steps.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

404.description: Not a session's id (no body)

502.description: The runner refused or didn't answer (`ok: false`)

get.summary:
A runner session's live stream, passed through from its runner as it comes (its steps, the
words as they are typed, its current step), from the step after `?after=`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only the steps after this one.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many (400 by default, 1000 at most).

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: A worker's: only this sub-agent call's steps.

200.description: A text/event-stream of the runner's events (`head`, `step`, `delta`, `think`, `tokens`)

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

404.description: Not a session's id (no body)

post.summary:
The person's reply in a runner session: its next turn (queued behind one that runs), with
their files put in its inbox first.

400.description: Nothing to send

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

404.description: Not a session's id (no body)

502.description: The runner refused or didn't answer (`ok: false`)

post.summary: Stops a runner session: it and the turns queued behind it.

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

404.description: Not a session's id (no body)

502.description: The runner refused or didn't answer (`ok: false`)

post.summary: Stops the turn a runner session is in; its queued turns carry on.

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

404.description: Not a session's id (no body)

502.description: The runner refused or didn't answer (`ok: false`)

post.summary: Changes a runner session's model, effort or title, as the body asks.

requestBody.description: `{ model?, effort?, title? }`, passed to the runner as is

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

404.description: Not a session's id (no body)

502.description: The runner refused or didn't answer (`ok: false`)

post.summary:
Moves a runner session to another task, on a server that keeps plans: its link and its
open run go there, both tasks' histories say so, and a task made for the session that is
left with nothing of its own is put away.

400.description: No task in the body, or the task is done or archived

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

404.description: No such session (or not a session's id) or task, or a server that keeps no plans (`ok: false`)

get.summary:
A worker's steps, as a session's transcript: after `?after=`, the first `?limit=` (400 by
default, 1000 at most) of what came since; else the newest; `?agent=` keeps one sub-agent
call's.
get.description: Without a worker runtime, every id is 404 `no such task`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only the steps after this one.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many (400 by default, 1000 at most).

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: A worker's: only this sub-agent call's steps.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

404.description: No such task (`ok: false`; no body for an id that isn't a number)

get.summary:
A worker's steps as they come: each new step, and its head whenever it changes, looked at
every second; a `: ping` every 15 s.
get.description: Without a worker runtime, every id is 404 `no such task`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only the steps after this one.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many (400 by default, 1000 at most).

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: A worker's: only this sub-agent call's steps.

200.description: A text/event-stream of `{ type: step, step }` and `{ type: head, session }`

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

404.description: No such task (`ok: false`; no body for an id that isn't a number)

post.summary: The person's reply to a worker: it carries on with it.
post.description: Without a worker runtime, every id is 404 `no such task`.

400.description: Nothing to send

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

404.description: No such task (`ok: false`; no body for an id that isn't a number)

409.description: The worker didn't take it (`ok: false`)

post.summary: Stops a worker.
post.description: Without a worker runtime, every id is 404 `no such task`.

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

404.description: No such task (`ok: false`; no body for an id that isn't a number)

post.summary: Stops a worker (a worker has no turn of its own to interrupt: the same as stop).
post.description: Without a worker runtime, every id is 404 `no such task`.

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

404.description: No such task (`ok: false`; no body for an id that isn't a number)

get.summary:
Every background job running now on the runners' machines: the runners' sessions with a
turn on, and the runs and scheduled jobs each runner lists of its machine.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary: Stops a job (`{ id }`): a session on its runner, a run by its runner.

400.description: Gone, not one to stop from here, or its runner refused (`ok: false`)

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

get.summary: The assistant's MCP servers and skills, each with its state and the person's switch.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary:
Turns a server or skill on or off (`{ kind: mcp | skill, name, on }`), or reconnects a
server (`{ kind: reconnect, name }`): the page after it.

400.description: Not a change that can be made

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

get.summary: Every place the assistant works and connection it reads through, live.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary: Looks at one place again now (`{ id, kind: check }`): the page after it.

400.description: Not an action this page has

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

get.summary:
Every account the runners use, each with its machine and use, and the account the
assistant runs on.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary:
Pins the assistant to an account (`{ account }`), or `auto` (or nothing) to let it run on
the one with the most room: the assistant's account after it, and the Usage card.

400.description: Not an account the assistant runs on (`ok: false`)

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

post.summary:
Asks every runner to look at its accounts' use now, in the background (at most once in 2
minutes); the state's `usage` brings the numbers as they land.

401.description: Sign-in is enforced and there is no session

post.summary:
Starts recording a call on the owner's Mac (`action` anything but `stop`), or stops it. The
transcript goes to `room`. Always 200: `ok: false` with
`error` when the Mac didn't do it or the call couldn't be kept.

200.description: What the Mac's recorder said, or why it (or the server) didn't

400.description: A body the route refuses

401.description: No signed-in device (in either auth mode)

post.summary:
One track of a call the Mac recorded, its audio (m4a) as the body; `last` queues the call
to be transcribed (and ends its live copilot).

parameters.name: call
parameters.description:
The call's id: 6 to 40 letters, digits, `_` and `-`. A call the server doesn't know
(started on the Mac itself) is made, in Main.

thread.description: The thread it is in, if any (Slack's thread timestamp).

from.description: Who said it, as the channel names them.

ts.description: The message's own id in the channel (Slack's message timestamp), if it has one.

user.description:
The channel's id for who said it (a Slack user id, an app's email for them), if it has
one: the bridge's word, which proves nobody's identity.

channelName.description: The channel's name, as people know it (`#launch`), if it has one.

files.description: The files shared with it, as the channel names them.

direct.description: It is a direct message to the agent (a message in an app's chat always counts as one).

InboundNote.description:
`POST /api/agents/{id}/notes`: a note from the agent's bridge about the bridge itself (its
connection was down and is back, a button on one of the agent's own messages was tapped),
not from anyone in a channel. It is no one's request and never an approval.

InboundReply.description: What became of an inbound message or a bridge's note.

turn.description: It became a turn in the agent's room.

skipped.description: Why it did not, when it did not.

InstallId.description:
This installation of a client: made once and kept with its session, so signing in again on
the same device replaces that device's row on the server instead of adding one.

Written out rather than by the text-id macro only for its validation rule; its API is the
other text ids'.

Issue.description:
A task, as the state lists them: its own fields and, from the board, its effective deadline
and its score.

key.description: Its key, as shown: the server's task-key prefix followed by the task's number.

owner.description: Who does it: the person's or the assistant's id.

oneOf.description: Its goal, when it has one of its own.
Its project.
When it is due.
An ask: the day to decide it by.
What it asks, when it waits on a decision.

action.description: What the person should do, one line, when it waits on them.

oneOf.description: When it was done.
Its parent, for a subtask.
Its deadline, or its project's.

hardDeadline.description: Whether that deadline is someone else's (hard).

score.description: How much it matters now: Today is ranked by it.

parkedUntil.description: Out of sight until then (a day or an instant).

oneOf.description: When it was made.

last.description: The newest line of its history.

tracked.description: Done elsewhere: the assistant only keeps its status, no worker takes it.

body.description: The person's notes on it, or the brief the assistant's worker works from.

hard.description: Its own deadline (`due`) is someone else's (hard).

oneOf.description: How long it takes.

progress.description: A counted task: how many are done so far.

total.description: A counted task: how many there are in all.

unit.description: A counted task: what is counted (`episodes`).

oneOf.description: A parent: its subtasks at a glance.

eta.description: The assistant's estimate, in words (`about 2 hours`).

ultra.description: Its next run splits the work across many agents (ultra mode).

oneOf.description: Its sub-agents at a glance, when it has any.

What is actually happening on it, from its runs: what a client shows, rather than its
status, which is the assistant's intent. Older servers don't send it.

kind.description: `finding` for a finding (a scan's or a review's result filed under it); none for a task.

oneOf.description: A finding: whether its fix landed.
A finding: the task that fixes it.
Its project's area, when it is in one.
The person's own message that asked for it, its own or its parent's.
Someone other than the person asked for it, its own or its parent's.
What the person's last tap on its send card came to.
Its plan at a glance, on a server that keeps plans (empty: no plan yet).

place.description: The machine it runs on, in words (`Linux PC`, `Mac`).

name.description: Its name there (a unit's, a process's).

what.description: What it is, in a word or two (`Codex run`, `Worker`).

oneOf.description: The task it works for.
When it started.
When it ended.

cpu.description: Its CPU now, in % of one core.

oneOf.description: What it last said or did.
Its last file change.
Its last sign of life.

stop.description: It can be stopped from the app.

clear.description: It failed and can be taken off the list.

JobActivity.description: What a job last said or changed.

text.description: What it said, or the file it changed.

oneOf.description: When.

JobId.description: A background job the assistant started (its own id, such as `b1a2`).

JobKind.description: One of: worker, unit, server, service, process, session, launchd. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

JobState.description: One of: running, starting, failed, exited. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

JobsMac.description: Whether the Mac's runner answered, and why not.

Landed.description: One of: landed, partly, not_landed, superseded, unchecked. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

LastCall.description: The phone's report of the last call, as the state shows it.

report.description: When it ended, how long it was and what the phone said of it.

transcript.description: The start of what was said (2000 characters at most).

LatestBuilds.description:
The newest build reported per platform: `null` where none was. The server writes
both fields always.

Lesson.description: A standing rule the person agreed to.

LessonId.description: A standing rule the person agreed to.

LineKind.description: One of: turn, say, steer. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

LinkKind.description: One of: thread, ticket, chat. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

LinkStatementRequest.description:
`POST /api/connect/link-statement`: which account the machine should sign a link statement
for, at which relay.

account.description: The account's user id: 1 to 255 characters of visible ASCII.

relayDomain.description: The relay's domain, in its normal form.

Listing.description:
A runner's listing passed through (folders: `{ machine, home, recent, documents, projects }`
or `{ machine, home, path, git, folders }`; branches: `{ repo, current, branches }`).

The server relays it as the runner sends it; [`crate::runner::new_session::FolderList`] describes the same wire.

Live.description: What the assistant is doing while it works in a room.

text.description: The answer so far. May stay empty until the final answer reaches the chat.

doing.description: Its current step, one plain line; none at the very start.

t.description: Seconds from the call's start it is about.

LiveCallLine.description: A line of a call's live transcript.

who.description: Who said it: the owner or the other side.

LiveCheckin.description: The check-in that names a scheduled task.

oneOf.description: What the assistant is doing while it works in a room.

text.description: The answer so far. May stay empty until the final answer reaches the chat.

doing.description: Its current step, one plain line; none at the very start.

LiveLast.description: The last run that ended on a task.

oneOf.description: When it ended.

LiveRun.description: The run open on a task.

place.description: That machine in words (`the Mac`); older servers don't send it.

worker.description: It is the task's own worker.

oneOf.description: When it was sent.
When it started; none while queued.

LiveState.description: One of: running, queued, scheduled, waiting, stalled, todo, parked, held, done, canceled. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

LiveWatch.description: The watch that looks at a scheduled task.

every.description: How often it looks, in minutes.

oneOf.description: When it saw that.

Loop.description: An open loop the assistant keeps: someone waiting on the person, a promise, a deadline.

due.description: When it is due (a day or an instant), if it is.

source.description: Where it came from, in words.

chat.description: The chat it lives in, when known.

oneOf.description: When it was last touched.
The person wrote in its chat after it opened: it may be answered.
The room that opened it, when it isn't Main.

LoopLag.description: The lag now and over the last minute and five, in whole milliseconds.

p95_1m.description: The 95th percentile of the last minute's samples (0 without any).

max_1m.description: The longest of the last minute.

p95_5m.description: The 95th percentile of the last five minutes' samples.

max_5m.description: The longest of the last five minutes.

LoopReport.description:
`GET /api/loop`'s answer: the lag, and the slow work of the last five minutes, the longest
in all first.

MacStatus.description:
The Mac's row: whether its helper answers, and if so whether the screen is locked and how
long the Mac has been idle.

Written as `{ "online": false }` alone when the helper doesn't
answer, and `{ "online": true, "locked": …, "idle": … }` when it does, with `idle` `null` when
the helper doesn't say.

locked.description: The screen is locked; only when `online`.

idle.description:
Seconds since the last mouse or key input on the Mac; only when `online`, and `null` when
the helper doesn't say.

host.description: Its host name, as its runner reports it.

status.description: Its state in words (`ok`, `no sample for 3 min`).

oneOf.description: When its last sample came.

age.description: How old that sample is, in seconds.

placeable.description: Whether a new session may start there.

oneOf.description: Its processors.
Its memory.
Its battery, on a laptop.
Its runner's own figures.

history.description:
Its last day, in 5-minute points (each the worst of its samples), oldest first; `[]` when
it has none. Left out with `?history=0`.

MachineId.description: A machine that runs sessions, as its runner names itself (for example `runner`).

MachineIdentity.description: A machine's id and its Ed25519 public key, which must have that id.

id.description: The machine's id: 32 characters of lowercase base32.

publicKey.description: The machine's Ed25519 public key, base64url without padding; it must have that id.

MachineJobId.description:
A job running on one of the machines, as the jobs list names it (`unit:<name>`,
`pid:<n>`, `session:<id>`).

used5h.description: That account's use of its 5-hour window, 0 to 1.

used7d.description: That account's use of its week, 0 to 1.

oneOf.description: That account is out until then.

MachineState.description: One of: ok, warn, low, stale, offline, unknown. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

oneOf.description: The limits the states and warnings are judged by.

source.description: Where it is configured (`user`: the person's own configuration).

kind.description: How it runs: `stdio`, `http`, `sse`, a hosted connector.

fixed.description: The assistant's own tools: always on, no switch.

note.description: A line on what to do about it (how to sign in), or why it can't be switched.

McpState.description: One of: connected, failed, needs-auth, pending, disabled, off, unknown. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

pressure.description: The system's memory pressure, where it has one (`normal`, `warn`, `critical`).

MessageId.description: A chat message. Ids grow with time within the whole chat, so they order a room's messages.

MessageRef.description:
What an answer is about, as a chip under it: a task, a pull request, a report, a card or a
ticket. Only the fields of its kind are sent.

label.description: The chip's text: a task's key, `PR #3` or `Report`.

oneOf.description: The task it is about.

title.description: A longer name (the task's title, the repository).

MessageTo.description: One of: assistant, worker, session. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

Moment.description: One step of a task's history.

who.description:
Who: the person's id, the assistant's, or `worker`; empty when the server has none
(it may send `null`).

text.description: What happened, or what was said; empty when the server has none (it may send `null`).

MoveSession.description:
`POST .../task`: move the session to another task, on a server that keeps plans. Its link
and its open run go to `task`, and both tasks' histories say so; a task the server made for
the session that is left with nothing of its own is put away (`Merged into T-n`). 404 for a
session or a task the server doesn't know (and on a server that doesn't keep plans), 400 for
a task that is done or archived, each with an [`ErrorBody`](crate::error::ErrorBody).

task.description: The task it works for from now on.
The task it works for now.

id.description: Its id: 1 to 40 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, not starting with `-`.

persona.description: Its system prompt, up to 50,000 characters.

principal.description: Who it works for, 1 to 120 characters.

oneOf.description: Its room; none: the server makes one named after it.
The project it is scoped to.
Its monthly cap, with its currency.

enabled.description: Whether it starts enabled (yes when left out).

workerShell.description:
Whether its tasks' workers may run shell commands, as the server's user (no when left
out): for an agent the owner trusts.

NewParty.description: `POST /api/parties`: a new party, started at once.

topic.description: The topic or opening line, 4,000 characters at most.

maxTurns.description: The turn cap (the server keeps it within 1 to 100).

maxTokens.description: The token cap (the server keeps it within 5,000 to 2,000,000).

title.description: Its title; the topic's start when none.

NewSession.description:
`POST /api/runner/sessions`: one of the person's own sessions, on the machine and in the
folder they picked, with their first message.

The server relays it as the runner sends it; [`crate::runner::new_session::OpenSession`] describes the same wire.

files.description: Files sent with it (uploads of the chat).

account.description: The account to run on (the runner picks when none is given).

worktree.description: `true` or `{ branch?, base? }` for a worktree of its own, passed to the runner as is.

NewSessionReply.description:
`POST /api/runner/sessions`'s answer: the runner's session, its id and the first turn's id.

The server relays it as the runner sends it; [`crate::runner::new_session::OpenedSession`] describes the same wire.

session.description: The session, as the runner answered.

NewTaskRequest.description:
`POST /api/tasks`: a program on the server's machine hands the assistant a job the person
asked it for. Only with the server's program key.

title.description: Its title (the first 200 characters are kept).

body.description: Its brief (the first 20,000 characters are kept).

from.description: The program, in words (`a program` when left out).

at.description: When it was written (the writing device's clock: a note written offline keeps its time).

created.description: When the server first had it.

updated.description: When the server last changed it.

NoteAuthor.description: One of: owner, assistant. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

uid.description: The note's uid: a new one makes a note, a known one edits it.

text.description: What it says, trimmed by the server; empty deletes the note.

oneOf.description: When it was written; none (or a time in the future): now.
The note as saved; none when it was deleted (or there was nothing to delete).

NoteUid.description:
A quick note, made by the device that wrote it (8 to 64 letters, digits, `_` or `-`),
so sending it again changes nothing.

OkReply.description:
`{ "ok": true }`: the request was done. Some routes add fields of their own; this type reads
only `ok`.

PairRequest.description:
`POST /api/auth/pair`: a one-time code (made on a signed-in device) for a session of this
device's own.

code.description:
The code as typed: case, spaces and the dash don't matter (`abcd efgh` is `ABCD-EFGH`).
Not blank, at most 32 characters (a code is 8, shown as 9 with its dash).

oneOf.description:
This installation: the same install pairing again keeps its device row. Left out, or
empty, the device gets a new row each time it pairs .

name.description:
The device's name in the device list; left out, null or empty, "A device". At most 60
UTF-16 units; longer is refused.

model.description:
The kind of device (`macOS`, `linux`, `Pixel 8`); may be left out or null. At most 40
UTF-16 units.

publicKey.description:
The device's own Ed25519 public key, base64url without padding, which the machine keeps
on the device's row. Clients that predate it leave it out.

PairingCode.description:
`POST /api/auth/pair/new`'s answer: a code for a new device, good once for 10 minutes.

The code is 8 characters from an alphabet without look-alikes (no 0/O, 1/I/L), shown as
`ABCD-EFGH`. A request that isn't from a signed-in device or the server's key is refused
with 401 and an `ErrorBody` (`ok: false`).

code.description: The code as shown to the person, `ABCD-EFGH`.

link.description:
The pairing link for the code (`https://emberhut.com/pair#id=…&code=…&route=…`), to show as
text and as a QR code, from a server that has a machine id. A server that predates it
(or a legacy host) leaves it out.

recent.description: The person's own personas from earlier parties, newest first, one per name.

models.description: The models a persona can talk with.

oneOf.description: The caps and model a new party starts with.

why.description: Why it paused or ended, in words.

cost.description: What it cost, in US dollars at list prices.

PartyLine.description: A line said in a party.

who.description: Who said it: a persona's id, or the person's (`owner`).

model.description: The model a persona's turn came from.

cost.description: What it cost, in US dollars.

in.description: US dollars per million tokens in.

out.description: US dollars per million tokens out.

note.description: What it is good for and what it costs, in words.

PartyPage.description: `GET /api/parties/{id}`: the party and its talk, oldest first.

PartyReply.description: The answer to a new party and to the person's controls.

oneOf.description: The party as it is now; `null` after a delete.

PartySay.description:
`POST /api/parties/{id}/say`: the person jumps in or steers. A party that waits starts
again to answer.

text.description: What they say, 4,000 characters at most.

PartyStatus.description: One of: running, paused, done, stopped. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

PersonChange.description:
`personSet`: whether a person's messages wake the assistant at once (instead of with its
next look, every 15 minutes).

important.description: Wake the assistant when they write.

Persona.description: A persona: in a party, among the presets, or one of the person's own.

role.description: Who they are and how they talk: their prompt's heart.

color.description: Its colour in a party (`blue`, `orange`, `green`, `purple`, `pink`); empty elsewhere.

PersonaId.description:
A persona: `p1` to `p5` in a party, a ready-made one's own id (`skeptic`) among the
presets, `recent1`… among the person's own from earlier parties.

steps.description: Every step in order: each top-level step, then its sub-steps.

summary.description: The plan at a glance, as the task's row shows it.

oneOf.description: The top-level step it is a sub-step of; none for a top-level step.

title.description: What the step is, one short line (`Build the Mac app`).

note.description: A note: what it came to, or what blocks it.

link.description: A link to what it produced (a pull request, a page, a file).

oneOf.description: When it was first worked on.
When it was done or skipped.

done.description: Steps done (sub-steps in place of the step they make up; skipped ones not counted).

total.description: Steps in all, counted the same way. 0: no plan yet.

oneOf.description: The step being worked on, or next.

blocker.description: What blocks the plan: the first blocked step's note, else its title.

eta.description: The agent's estimate of what is left, in words (`about 2 hours`).

oneOf.description: When the plan last changed; none while it is empty and never written.
A turn of work on the task ended while its plan was still empty: when the last one did.

Point.description: A 5-minute point of a machine's day: the worst of its samples.

oneOf.description: When.

vram.description: Peak GPU memory in use, in bytes.

PoliciesRequest.description: `PUT /api/agents/{id}/policies`: the agent's whole list of policies.

Policy.description: Who approves one kind of an agent's actions.

approver.description:
`owner`, `none` (no approval needed), or an approver's id. The fixed core's kinds are
only ever the owner's.

Preset.description: A preset, with its colours in both appearances.

ProbeAnswer.description:
`GET /api/connect/probe`'s answer: the machine's signature over the device's nonce and kind,
and over how, where and as what it was reached.

id.description: The machine's id: 32 characters of lowercase base32.

publicKey.description: The machine's Ed25519 public key, base64url without padding; it must have that id.

local.description:
The local socket address that accepted a direct connection, in its normal form; empty
when relayed, and only then.

host.description:
The request's host (or, relayed, the `host` of the relay's `Forwarded`), in its normal
form.

signature.description: The machine's signature over the `emberhut probe v1` statement, base64url without padding.

Project.description: A project: what tasks are grouped by. Its health comes from its hard deadlines.

oneOf.description: The goal it serves.
Its own deadline.

hard.description: Whether that deadline is someone else's.

oneOf.description: A paused project's day to come back.
Its health; none without a hard deadline.
The nearest deadline of its open tasks.

ProjectChange.description: `projectSet`: the fields given change, the rest stay.

priority.description: Its priority: 0 none, 1 urgent, 2 high, 3 medium, 4 low.

deadline.description: Its deadline: a day, or `null` for none.

oneOf.description: Active, paused, archived or done.
With `status` paused: the day it comes back.

ProjectHealth.description: One of: on_track, at_risk, late. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

ProjectKind.description: One of: deliverable, ongoing. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

ProjectStatus.description: One of: active, paused, archived, done. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

ProviderKind.description: One of: claude, anthropic, deepseek, openrouter, ollama, anthropic-compatible, openai, openai-compatible. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

id.description: Its id, as a request names it.

name.description: Its name for people, when the provider gives one.

ProviderRequest.description:
`PUT /api/agent/provider` and `POST /api/agent/provider/test`: a provider and what it needs.
Its `Debug` leaves the key out.

apiKey.description:
Its API key: needed by `anthropic`, `deepseek`, `openrouter`, `anthropic-compatible`
and `openai`, optional for `openai-compatible`, not taken by `claude` and `ollama`.
Surrounding whitespace is ignored.

baseUrl.description:
Where its API is: needed by `anthropic-compatible` (what the agent CLI is pointed at)
and `openai-compatible` (`https://…/v1`); for `deepseek` (`https://api.deepseek.com`),
`openrouter` (`https://openrouter.ai/api`), `ollama` (`http://localhost:11434`) and
`openai` (`https://api.openai.com/v1`) in place of their usual address; not taken by
`claude` and `anthropic`.

model.description:
The model the agent runs on, as the provider names it: needed by `openrouter`,
`ollama`, `anthropic-compatible`, `openai` and `openai-compatible` (to save; a test
takes none); none: the provider's default (`deepseek-v4-pro` for `deepseek`) or, for
`claude` and `anthropic`, the server's.

fastModel.description:
The model for quick side calls (titles, summaries, the guard's judge); none: the
provider's default (`deepseek-v4-flash` for `deepseek`) or `model`.

ProviderTest.description:
`POST /api/agent/provider/test`'s answer: the provider accepted what was sent (nothing is
saved), and the models it lists.

checked.description: The provider was asked: no for `claude`, which only the agent CLI itself can check.

models.description: The models it lists, as it lists them; empty when it lists none or wasn't asked.

token.description:
The push token: an iPhone's APNs device token (64 to 200 hex digits), or an Android
phone's FCM registration token (32 to 4096 letters, digits, `_`, `:` or `-`). Left out,
it is no token, and refused as one.

platform.description: `"android"` for an FCM token; left out for an iPhone.

env.description:
An iPhone's APNs service: `"production"` for a release build; anything else, or
nothing, is the sandbox (a development build). Not read for Android.

Quote.description: The message a reply quotes, as its bubble shows it.

oneOf.description: When it was said.
Its first picture or video.

call.description: The call's id (the recorder ends its live copilot by it).

RecordAction.description: Start or stop. Read leniently: `stop` stops, any other word starts.

text.description: What the server did, in its words, when it did.

RecordCallRequest.description: Start or stop recording a call.

action.description: What to do. The server reads anything but `stop` as `start`, and no action as `start`.

room.description: The room the transcript goes to; Main when left out.

RefKind.description: One of: task, pr, report, card, ticket, file. A newer server may send another word; clients keep it as it is.

RefreshRequest.description: `POST /api/auth/refresh`: a new access token for this device's refresh token.

refresh.description: The refresh token the last grant gave. Not blank.

oneOf.description:
This installation; a device signed in before it sent one gets it recorded here. Left
out or empty, none (as when pairing).

RefreshToken.description: The token that renews the access token. It turns over on every use.

ReportDone.description: A task finished this week, in the weekly report.

ReportGoal.description: A goal in the weekly report.

ReportProject.description: A project under its goal in the weekly report.

oneOf.description: Its health; none without a hard deadline.

Requested.description: The person's own request for a task: when, and the message and room it was made from.

oneOf.description: The message that asked; none for a task added in the app.
The room it was asked in.

RequestedBy.description: A task asked for by someone other than the person.

how.description: How it was marked as theirs, in words.

Rollup.description:
A parent's subtasks at a glance: how many are done (archived ones don't count), which wait on
the person, and their counts added up.

waiting.description: The subtasks waiting on the person.

progress.description: Their counts added up, when every subtask has one.

of.description: Their totals added up, when every subtask has one.

left.description: What the open ones still need, when each of them has a count.

RoomId.description: A room: Main, or one conversation per project.

RoomRow.description:
One room's line in the switcher: what waits there and the last thing said.

The server sends Main first, then the rooms by their last activity, then the quiet ones by
name.

Its project's goal.

active.description: Whether its project is active (Main always is).

oneOf.description: A paused room's day to come back by itself.

unread.description: The assistant's messages there not seen yet (0 while paused or archived).

needs.description: The tasks waiting on the person there.
